blocks: Slot 35's pattern A stores velocities 9, 24, 25, 18 and so on, and MIDI out sent the same values, although this preset's sound ignores velocity.
Ties: slot 113 D3 Chords sends its first chord once and holds it for 1.5 steps; the next step lists those notes under held.

Selecting a slot loads pattern A. Slot 395 stores notes only in pattern B, and its audition produced no notes and no sound. No CC, program change or SysEx message is known that switches to pattern B; MIDI Song Select 1 (F3 01) left pattern A playing. Freakout's notes record that changing the values after pattern A in a saved preset did not select B either.

To audition pattern B, select the slot on the panel, press B, and run the task with --no-select. Without the panel, write a copy of the preset with B's steps in A's place to a spare slot; Microfreak/Sequence/Research records this for slot 446.

The recording is normalized to its peak before analysis. Each step's window starts 12 ms after the step and lasts up to one step or 400 ms. YIN gives the strongest pitch. The chord estimate scores every note from MIDI 24 to 96 by the spectrum at its first 20 harmonics, keeps the best, subtracts a smoothed copy of that note's harmonics, and repeats until a note scores under 35% of the first.

MIDI out records the notes the sequencer played. The audio shows what the instrument sounds, which can differ from the notes it sends: slot 374 sounds every second step an octave below the note on MIDI out, with a clean, periodic tone, so those steps read octave.

Single notes come out reliably on slots 5, 35 and 374. Chords come out partly: the estimate misses chord notes and adds neighbouring ones, especially with detuned oscillators such as SuperWave. Onsets come out weak for soft attacks and legato, so onset can be false on a played step; the pitch comparison does not depend on it.

The modulation tracks keep sending their CCs during playback and replace the values --plain sent before Start; the report warns about this. On slot 35, whose tracks send CC 12, 13, 23 and 83, --plain did not raise agreement.
Each run used the defaults (120 BPM, two loops), with nobody at the panel.
Microfreak/Preset/005 MotivSeq: 64 steps of 1/16, 128 notes on MIDI out, identical in both loops. The audio pitch agreed on all 128 steps.

Microfreak/Preset/035 FM Seq: 16 steps of 1/16 with 3 rests per loop. The audio agreed on 23 of 26 played steps and heard an octave error on the other 3, all C1 or C2 FM bass notes. The 6 rest steps were silent.

Microfreak/Preset/113 D3 Chords: 64 steps of three- and four-note chords with ties, 248 notes on MIDI out. The chord estimate found every note in 28 of the 80 played steps and, on average, 73% of the notes and 84% of the pitch classes.
Microfreak/Preset/374 TMF.24.12.04.A: 16 steps of 1/8, 12 clocks per step, no note between steps. Half the steps agreed and half sounded an octave lower, as Audio analysis describes.
Microfreak/Preset/395 26.06.25: an empty pattern A, so no notes and no sound, as Pattern A and B describes.
After each run, Arp/Seq MIDI Out read back as off. Clock Source stayed on USB.

mise run microfreak:inspect reads a preset I already saved and prints its named parameters as JSON. It uses only Python's standard library, opens no MIDI port and leaves the file unchanged.
Keep the exports outside the repository: the presets are mine and the repository is public.
A .bin from microfreak:download: the 35-value saved header plus the 4672-value payload, or the payload alone.
A .mfpz preset export from MIDI Control Center: one text archive record in a ZIP. The report names the member as exported.

A .mfprojz project export with --slot N: the inspector picks the one .mbp whose leading slot number and final bank/slot suffix match, and refuses ambiguous banks. Project slot numbers describe the project on the computer, which can differ from what is on the instrument.
ZIP members are read in memory with a size limit and never extracted.
status: raw_parameters, SHA-256 digests of the record and the payload, and the named fields.

Each field keeps its stored three values as raw_hex, the first as descriptor, and the other two read as signed and as unsigned little-endian integers. These readings preserve what is stored; they don't give the value the instrument's display shows. Descriptor meanings and display conversions are marked unverified.
The values are the saved base settings. Modulation, performance gestures and unsaved edits can change what I hear.
VCF.Cutoff, VCF.Reso and VCO.Type match the control names in Microfreak/UG/21 Appendix D - CC Values.

The oscillator has three physical controls, Wave, Timbre and Shape (Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/02 Param Controls), and Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types says what each does per oscillator: Wavetable uses Table, Position and Chorus; Sample uses Start, Length and Loop; Two Op.FM uses Ratio, Amount and Shape. The inspector reports Wave, Timbre and Shape as candidate names for the stored VCO.Param1, VCO.Param2 and VCO.Param3, because the manual names neither those stored fields nor their conversions.
An initialized .mbp gives status: initialized and no fields.

An unknown layout gives status: unsupported_layout, the position where parsing stopped and the digests, and exits with status 2. Invalid input also exits 2. A failed parse returns no partial list. Keep the original file when the layout is unsupported.
--interpret-fw5 adds an interpretation layer next to the raw report:

It assumes MicroFreak firmware 5. Exports don't record the firmware, so interpretations.firmware_detected_from_export is false. Initialized presets and unsupported layouts keep their status and get no interpretations.

interpretations names the oscillator model and what its Wave, Timbre and Shape controls do, where supported. Firmware 5 numbers its saved engines from 1: SuperWave is 2, Wavetable is 3 and Vocoder is 14. Each interpreted field has a kind, a value, a range and evidence ids, and evidence_sources maps those ids to the research or manual page behind them. The raw fields, digests and status stay as they are.

The formulas and engine order come from Freakout's firmware notes and its structured-payload parser, implemented in lib/semantics.py. Control names per oscillator follow Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types. An unknown oscillator value keeps a null model and generic field labels; values outside the supported ranges stay raw_only.

Fields whose conversion was measured on the instrument also get display: the value the panel shows, its unit and a short text, such as ±12 semitones for VCO.BendRng or 4 voices for Gen.UniCnt. Microfreak/Patch/Storage lists those conversions.

normalized_0_1, normalized_minus_1_1 and metadata_scaled_integer name numeric ranges. They don't give the display's hertz, milliseconds or percentages, so display_conversions stays unverified. Matrix destinations and the identity of referenced samples or wavetables are not decoded. The option doesn't change preset pages or handwritten notes.
--sequence adds both sequencer patterns, decoded by lib/sequence.py:

The sequence object holds the shared length, gate length and smoothing, and for patterns A and B: whether the pattern is in use, its modulation-track destinations, and one entry per played step with its status (note, tie, rest), notes, note names (C4 = MIDI 60), velocities and modulation values. Steps past the sequence length are counted, not listed.
Microfreak/Sequence/Write a sequence goes the other way: it writes a described sequence into a slot. Microfreak/Sequence/Storage has the layout and the experiments behind it.
How a saved preset is laid out
The text archive envelope follows Elektroid's MicroFreak serialization. Elektroid's preset connector moves the payload without decoding parameter names.
How a saved preset is laid out

The framing inside it was inferred from MIDI Control Center exports. A live slot read matched the whole payload of the matching export, and every populated record examined went through expansion and repacking unchanged. Most followed the named-field layout; one began with an unknown structure. The tests use synthetic data, so no private export is stored here.
How a saved preset is laid out
Each group of eight holds a mask of high bits followed by seven 7-bit values. Mask bit 0 is the first value's high bit, through bit 6 for the seventh. Expanding 4672 values gives 4088.
How a saved preset is laid out

The parameter block starts at expanded position 0. A tag's upper three bits say whether a section name (1), a field name (2) or a value (3) follows, and its lower five bits give how many values follow. Names are ASCII. In the supported layout a parameter value is three values long.
How a saved preset is laid out

0x40 closes a section and 0x20 closes the root. What follows the root is kept in the export and counted in the report but not interpreted: padding, stale fragments and, from expanded position 1980, the sequence patterns that --sequence decodes. It must not be parsed as more named fields.
How a saved preset is laid out

Labels seen so far: VCO oscillator controls, VCF filter, EG1 cycling envelope, EG2 main envelope, LFO, Kbd, Arp, Gen, Mat, matrix columns Co1–Co7, Seq and Voc. Fields vary between presets and format generations. Unknown or missing fields are never filled with defaults.
How a saved preset is laid out

The first stored value of each parameter often looks like a range or type descriptor and the other two like a normalized value. That is a hypothesis: oscillator descriptors vary between records, and modulation amounts may need a signed reading.
Converting the firmware 5 ranges to the values on the display needs paired display-and-export observations or more evidence about how presets are serialized. Matrix destinations are still undecoded.

Archive format versions and other envelope attributes are kept in the metadata. The envelope's version string is not assumed to be a firmware version. Export digests identify what is stored, not equivalent sounds, and don't show that referenced samples and wavetables were kept.

Garden full-preset download captures the header and sound data, with a manifest and checksums. The raw backup is a custom format, not an MCC-compatible .mfp or .mbp file. Initialized slots are rejected by this downloader, so backup support needs extending before a general CRUD tool can cover every slot.

Existing mise entry points are microfreak:sync, microfreak:download, microfreak:inspect, microfreak:compare and microfreak:upload. Inspection and comparison support examining exported preset data; microfreak:upload writes a downloaded preset to a slot (Microfreak/CLI/Upload a preset).
microfreak_preset_rename reads a saved preset header with operation 0x19, mode 0. The response uses operation 0x52.

The function edits the name in the returned header, sends the complete header using operation 0x52, then sends operation 0x52 with the preset address and mode 1. It finishes with a MIDI program change to select the renamed preset.
Rename sends the header without transferring the sound-data packets. A custom CLI should preserve every header field except the explicitly edited name or category.

Device slot addresses are zero-based; user-facing slots are 1–512. Name storage supports 14 characters. Elektroid accepts spaces, letters, digits, period, underscore and hyphen, replaces unsupported characters with periods, and truncates long names. A custom CLI could reject invalid input and show the accepted name before writing.

The protocol includes a sequence counter, response operation and payload length. The garden downloader already validates these and uses bounded response waits. A writer should additionally validate acknowledgments, slot identity and readback results.

Elektroid's rename selects the preset afterward. That can replace an unsaved edit in the active sound; device validation should determine whether selecting the preset is required for persistence or only for refreshing the display.
Read: names, categories and initialized status are already decoded by the garden inventory script.
Update name: directly supported by Elektroid's header write sequence.
Update category: the category field is present in the same writable header, making the rename sequence a plausible implementation. A category-only write and readback need testing on the instrument.
Create: import a complete preset or copy an existing preset into a chosen slot. Elektroid implements full preset upload; slots are fixed storage locations rather than newly allocated records.

Delete: reset a slot to an initialized preset. Elektroid can serialize and upload initialized presets, but its preset connector exposes no delete operation. The reset behavior and persistence need device testing before exposing deletion.
Notes, tags and provenance: retain these in the garden. The inspected header and connector expose no arbitrary text metadata fields for these annotations.

mise run microfreak:probe changes stored settings of a preset, writes the result to a slot, selects it and plays a short MIDI script into it while the Zoom H5/My Unit records. It prints one JSON report with the level, pitch and brightness of each note. I use it to find out what a stored field does by listening to two values of it side by side.
Close MIDI Control Center, connect the MicroFreak and the H5 by USB, and run the task from the garden root. Keep hands off the keys while it plays.

--base is the preset to start from: a slot number, which the task reads and leaves unchanged, or a .bin file from microfreak:download. Slot 359, Init, holds every field firmware 5 saves; an older preset can lack fields such as Kbd.Scale or EG2.Snap, and the task refuses to set a field the base lacks.

--slot is where the result goes. When the slot holds a preset, the task saves it first in a new timestamped folder under --backup-dir, so one test slot can be probed again and again. The preset is stored as Probe unless --name gives another name.
Slots 497–512 are my test slots. My own presets fill slots 1–320 and 350–402.
--set NAME=VALUE changes one stored field, by the name microfreak:inspect prints. Repeat it for more fields.
An integer is a choice: VCO.BendRng=2, Kbd.Scale=1. The task stores choice × 32767 ÷ the field's descriptor, the number of choices minus one, the way every saved preset does.
--set NAME=VALUE changes one stored field, by the name microfreak:inspect prints. Repeat it for more fields.
A decimal is a normalized value from 0 to 1, such as VCF.Cutoff=0.5, or from −1 to 1 for a matrix amount, such as Co1.LFO=-0.25.
--set NAME=VALUE changes one stored field, by the name microfreak:inspect prints. Repeat it for more fields.
raw:N stores N as it is, such as Mat.Assign1=raw:0x0d01.
--set NAME=VALUE changes one stored field, by the name microfreak:inspect prints. Repeat it for more fields.
The report's settings_changed gives each changed field's stored value before and after.
Without --script the task plays one note, C4 at velocity 100 for 1.5 seconds, then records one more second. --note, --velocity, --hold and --tail change it.
A script is a YAML or JSON list of timed events, in seconds from the start:

on and off take a note name (C4 is MIDI 60) or number. bend runs from −1 (full down) to 1 (full up). cc takes a controller number and value. pressure sends channel pressure (aftertouch) 0–127. to and over turn a bend, CC or pressure into a ramp, with CC and pressure values rounded to whole numbers. tail is how long the recording runs after the last event.
The messages go out on the MicroFreak's MIDI input channel, which the task reads from the instrument first.
played lists each event with the time it was sent.

notes has one summary per note: onset_latency_ms, peak_db and end_db in dB relative to the H5's full scale, pitch and midi_median from the YIN method with cents_from_note, the lowest and highest pitch heard during the note, and centroid_hz_median, the spectral centroid, which rises as the sound gets brighter.

A note's pitch and brightness come from its frames within 30 dB of its peak, so a decaying note's quiet tail stays out. Each frame's centroid counts only the spectrum within 40 dB of that frame's strongest component, which keeps the H5's noise floor out of it.
A sub-oscillator one octave down makes the waveform repeat at the sub's period, so pitch reads an octave low and cents_from_note near −1200.

--frames also prints frames, the recording measured every 10 ms with the same values. A frame quieter than −70 dBFS has only t and db, and a frame where no pitch was found has no f0_hz, midi or aperiodicity. --output saves the report with every frame. --wav-dir saves the recording. Both must be outside the repository.
Levels are absolute, so two runs compare directly when the H5's input gain stays the same between them.
Slot 359's sound with Gen.PrstVol (Preset Volume) at 0, 12 and 24 played C4 at −27.8, −22.3 and −16.3 dBFS: about half a decibel per step of the setting. The pitch read 60.002 each time.
